ground_truth_witness: Let V=F₃² and q(x,y)=x²+y². Its polar form is B((x,y),(u,v))=2xu+2yv, with matrix diag(2,2) and determinant 1 in F₃, so B is nondegenerate. Yet every nonzero square in F₃ equals 1: vectors with one nonzero coordinate have q=1, and those with two have q=2. Thus q has no nonzero isotropic vector.
ground_truth_flaw: Every even-dimensional finite-field vector space equipped with a quadratic form whose associated bilinear form is nondegenerate decomposes into mutually orthogonal hyperbolic pairs.
